"""Estimate elastic modulus from tensile test data.

For each material we fit a straight line (stress = E * strain + b) to the
elastic region of every specimen, then report the per-material modulus as the
mean +/- standard deviation of the specimen slopes. A pooled fit over all
points of a material is reported as a cross-check.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DATA = HERE / "measurements.csv"
FIGURE = HERE / "modulus_analysis.png"
RESULTS = HERE / "results.csv"

MATERIAL_ORDER = ["aluminum", "steel", "titanium"]
COLORS = {"aluminum": "#1f77b4", "steel": "#d62728", "titanium": "#2ca02c"}


def linear_fit(strain, stress):
    """Return (slope, intercept, r_squared) for stress = slope*strain + intercept."""
    slope, intercept = np.polyfit(strain, stress, 1)
    predicted = slope * strain + intercept
    ss_res = np.sum((stress - predicted) ** 2)
    ss_tot = np.sum((stress - np.mean(stress)) ** 2)
    r_squared = 1.0 - ss_res / ss_tot
    return slope, intercept, r_squared


def main():
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA)

    rows = []
    for (material, specimen), group in df.groupby(["material", "specimen"]):
        strain = group["strain"].to_numpy()
        stress = group["stress_mpa"].to_numpy()
        slope, intercept, r_squared = linear_fit(strain, stress)
        rows.append(
            {
                "material": material,
                "specimen": specimen,
                "modulus_mpa": slope,
                "modulus_gpa": slope / 1000.0,
                "intercept_mpa": intercept,
                "r_squared": r_squared,
                "n_points": len(group),
            }
        )

    per_specimen = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["material", "specimen"])

    summary = (
        per_specimen.groupby("material")
        .agg(
            modulus_gpa_mean=("modulus_gpa", "mean"),
            modulus_gpa_std=("modulus_gpa", "std"),
            n_specimens=("specimen", "nunique"),
        )
        .reindex(MATERIAL_ORDER)
        .reset_index()
    )

    pooled_rows = []
    for material in MATERIAL_ORDER:
        group = df[df["material"] == material]
        slope, intercept, r_squared = linear_fit(
            group["strain"].to_numpy(), group["stress_mpa"].to_numpy()
        )
        pooled_rows.append(
            {
                "material": material,
                "pooled_modulus_gpa": slope / 1000.0,
                "pooled_intercept_mpa": intercept,
                "pooled_r_squared": r_squared,
            }
        )
    pooled = pd.DataFrame(pooled_rows)

    summary = summary.merge(pooled, on="material")
    per_specimen.to_csv(RESULTS, index=False)

    # --- figure: one panel per material, specimens as points, fits as lines ---
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5), sharex=True)
    for ax, material in zip(axes, MATERIAL_ORDER):
        subset = per_specimen[per_specimen["material"] == material]
        group_all = df[df["material"] == material]
        strain_min = group_all["strain"].min()
        strain_max = group_all["strain"].max()
        x_line = np.linspace(strain_min, strain_max, 100)

        for _, spec_row in subset.iterrows():
            specimen = spec_row["specimen"]
            points = df[df["specimen"] == specimen]
            ax.scatter(
                points["strain"],
                points["stress_mpa"],
                s=28,
                color=COLORS[material],
                alpha=0.7,
                label=specimen,
                zorder=3,
            )
            y_line = spec_row["modulus_mpa"] * x_line + spec_row["intercept_mpa"]
            ax.plot(x_line, y_line, color=COLORS[material], lw=1.5, alpha=0.85)

        mean_gpa = summary.loc[summary["material"] == material, "modulus_gpa_mean"].iloc[0]
        std_gpa = summary.loc[summary["material"] == material, "modulus_gpa_std"].iloc[0]
        ax.set_title(f"{material.capitalize()}\nE = {mean_gpa:.1f} +/- {std_gpa:.1f} GPa")
        ax.set_xlabel("strain (-)")
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, title="specimen")

    axes[0].set_ylabel("stress (MPa)")
    fig.suptitle("Tensile stress-strain data and linear elastic fits", fontsize=14)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.96))
    fig.savefig(FIGURE, dpi=150)
    print(f"wrote {FIGURE.name} and {RESULTS.name}")
    print(summary.to_string(index=False))
    print()
    print(per_specimen.to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.content:
# Elastic modulus from tensile tests

## Data

`measurements.csv` contains stress–strain measurements for three materials —
aluminum, steel, and titanium — with three specimens each (`AL-1..3`,
`ST-1..3`, `TI-1..3`) and ten strain points per specimen (strain up to 0.002).
All points fall in the linear elastic region, so the elastic (Young's) modulus
is the slope of a straight-line fit `stress = E · strain + b`.

## Method

For every specimen I fit `stress = E · strain + b` by least squares. The
per-material modulus is reported as the **mean ± standard deviation of the three
specimen slopes**. A pooled fit over all points of a material is given as a
cross-check; because the design is balanced (same strain grid and count for every
specimen), the pooled slope is identical to the mean of the specimen slopes.

## Results

| Material | E (GPa) | ± std | Specimens | Pooled R² |
|----------|--------:|------:|:---------:|:---------:|
| Aluminum | 69.4 | 1.8 | 3 | 0.9983 |
| Steel    | 199.1 | 2.0 | 3 | 0.9984 |
| Titanium | 116.6 | 1.7 | 3 | 0.9979 |

Per-specimen fits (slope = modulus, intercept should be ≈ 0 for an ideal test):

| Specimen | E (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|----------|--------:|----------------:|----:|
| AL-1 | 70.1 | −0.8 | 0.9995 |
| AL-2 | 67.4 | +0.9 | 0.9988 |
| AL-3 | 70.6 | −1.0 | 0.9991 |
| ST-1 | 201.2 | −1.5 | 0.9988 |
| ST-2 | 197.3 | +1.2 | 0.9986 |
| ST-3 | 198.7 | +2.2 | 0.9984 |
| TI-1 | 114.6 | −0.0 | 0.9978 |
| TI-2 | 117.8 | −2.2 | 0.9985 |
| TI-3 | 117.2 | −0.1 | 0.9987 |

Full numeric output is in `results.csv`.

## Figure

![Stress–strain data with linear elastic fits](modulus_analysis.png)

Each panel shows one material; markers are the measured points per specimen and
the lines are the individual linear fits. The fits overlay the data almost
exactly, consistent with R² > 0.997 everywhere.

## Discussion

- The estimated moduli — **≈69 GPa (Al), ≈199 GPa (steel), ≈117 GPa (Ti)** —
  agree well with typical handbook values (~70, ~200, ~116 GPa), which is a good
  sign the elastic region was captured cleanly.
- Scatter between specimens is small (std ≈ 2 GPa, i.e. under 2 %), and the
  regression intercepts are within a couple of MPa of zero, so the tests show
  little of the offset you would expect from preload or gauge misalignment.
- A single straight line describes each material very well over this strain
  range; no curvature is visible, so these points are all safely below yield.

## Files

- `analyze.py` — analysis and plotting script
- `modulus_analysis.png` — data + fits figure
- `results.csv` — per-specimen fit results
- `report.md` — this write-up
